human_name: NCF1 + NCF1B + NCF1C (p47phox) gene/pseudogene cluster at 7q11.23

GRCh38.note: Three paralogs dispersed across 7q11.23: NCF1B chr7:73,220,646-73,235,790 (+), NCF1 chr7:74,773,975-74,789,376 (+), NCF1C chr7:75,156,639-75,172,044 (-). Region also contains the Williams-Beuren-syndrome LCR cluster. NCF1 paralogs are ~15 kb each, embedded in the WBS LCR-A/B/C blocks. Intra-paralog identity >98% (Heyworth 2002, Roesler 2010).

copy_count_typical: 3 diploid wild-type (1 NCF1 + 1 NCF1B + 1 NCF1C); CNV reported (1-4) — see Brunson 2010
architecture_note: NCF1 cluster sits inside the Williams-Beuren syndrome (WBS) LCR architecture at 7q11.23. NCF1 itself is functional; NCF1B (at chr7:73.2 Mb, +strand) and NCF1C (at chr7:75.2 Mb, -strand) are pseudogenes carrying the signature 'GT' deletion at the start of exon 2 (Vázquez 2001; Heyworth 2002). The pathogenic CGD allele arises via GENE CONVERSION transferring the pseudogene ΔGT into functional NCF1, NOT via NAHR deletion of NCF1 itself. >90% of NCF1-CGD alleles carry this ΔGT.

position.note: exact CDS offset varies by transcript annotation; canonical position is the dinucleotide GT at the very start of exon 2

discriminating_snps.consequence: frameshift (premature stop); ΔGT = pseudogene-style allele = loss of p47phox protein
discriminating_snps.source: Vázquez N et al. 2001 Exp Hematol 29:234-243 (doi:10.1016/s0301-472x(00)00646-9); Heyworth PG, Noack D, Cross AR 2002 Blood 100:1845-1851 (doi:10.1182/blood-2002-03-0861)
discriminating_snps.note: THE diagnostic PSV for the locus. Functional NCF1 carries GTGT; both pseudogenes (NCF1B, NCF1C) carry GT (the dinucleotide deletion). Pathogenic CGD alleles are gene-converted NCF1 copies that now carry the pseudogene-style GT. Detection at short-read level is confounded by inter-paralog identity — this is the canonical example of why paralog-aware mapping matters clinically.

diagnostic_features.psv_strategy_note: Frontiers Immunol 2025 (Hoffmeister et al., doi:10.3389/fimmu.2025.1640496) describe a reliable HTS workflow for NCF1 ΔGT detection using paralog-specific long-range PCR + amplicon sequencing; their Figure 1 / Supplementary Table 1 list additional PSV positions distinguishing NCF1 from NCF1B / NCF1C across exons 1-11. For LLmap T1, the ΔGT in exon 2 is the dominant clinical PSV; downstream tools may want to also catalogue the ~30 additional inter-paralog differences across the 15 kb unit (intronic + synonymous), which can be cross-referenced to that paper's supplementary.

gene_conversion_disease_mechanism.process: Inter-locus gene conversion transferring the ΔGT (2 bp deletion) from NCF1B/NCF1C INTO functional NCF1
gene_conversion_disease_mechanism.implication: NCF1-CGD is the prototype gene-conversion-disease locus; clinical interpretation must distinguish 'true ΔGT in NCF1' vs 'sequencing-artifact mismapped pseudogene read'

primary.note: k=25 / mm=2 over the 15 kb unit. The exon-2 GTGT-vs-GT diagnostic site sits in a region where flanking unique anchors are within ~1-2 kb. Mapping MUST treat the three paralogs as distinct contigs and require junction-anchored reads for confident NCF1-vs-NCF1B/C assignment. Short-read calling at NCF1 without paralog awareness is unreliable (Hoffmeister 2025).

fallback_chain.name: anchor_walk
fallback_chain.rationale: walk from nearest unique anchor (GTF2IRD2 vs GTF2IRD2B flanking) into the NCF1/NCF1B/NCF1C unit; junction-anchored placement is the only reliable paralog call

fallback_chain.name: multi_position
fallback_chain.rationale: expected — report all three NCF1-paralog candidates when read cannot be anchored

fallback_chain.name: llm_checkpoint
fallback_chain.trigger: gene-conversion product suspected (ΔGT in NCF1 background)
fallback_chain.rationale: evaluate flanking SNPs against canonical NCF1 vs pseudogene patterns to distinguish true CGD allele from mismapped pseudogene read

fallback_chain.name: novel_haplotype_flag
fallback_chain.rationale: report 'NCF1 cluster — paralog ambiguous, manual review' for curator review

test_cases.note: HG002 wild-type at NCF1 cluster; useful negative control
Synthetic placeholder for an NCF1-CGD patient with biallelic ΔGT in NCF1 — expect short-read mapper without paralog awareness to undercall this; LLmap should detect via flanking-anchor walk

primary_sources.note: Vázquez N, Lehrnbecher T, Chen R et al. — Mutational analysis of patients with p47-phox-deficient chronic granulomatous disease: The significance of recombination events between the p47-phox gene (NCF1) and its highly homologous pseudogenes. Exp Hematol 29:234-243. (Task originally cited 'Vázquez 2001' as PNAS; the matching paper is Exp Hematol.) Defines the GTGT-vs-GT signature.

Heyworth PG, Noack D, Cross AR — Identification of a novel NCF-1 (p47-phox) pseudogene not containing the signature GT deletion: significance for A47° CGD carrier detection. Blood 100:1845-1851. (Task originally cited 'Roesler 2010'; the canonical GT-pseudogene paper is Heyworth 2002 — a later Roesler paper exists on CGD genotype-phenotype but the architecture reference is Heyworth.) Confirms three-paralog architecture and the diagnostic complications.

Hoffmeister F et al. — Reliable genetic diagnosis of NCF1 (p47phox)-deficient CGD using high-throughput sequencing. Front Immunol. Modern paralog-aware HTS workflow; supplementary tables contain PSVs across the 15 kb unit.

supporting_databases: UCSC genomicSuperDups (hg38) — captures the NCF1 / NCF1B / NCF1C WBS-LCR architecture
T2T-CHM13 v2.0 SD-BED (Vollger 2022) — resolves all three paralogs
HPRC R2 pangenome — haplotype-level WBS-LCR variation
provenance.db_coverage_note: Well represented in UCSC + OMIM + ClinGen. Inter-paralog identity ~98% over 15 kb means short-read PSV-only calling is fragile; long-read / WBS-anchored mapping (Paraphase, LLmap) is the appropriate tool.
